result.title: Using Transformers for Teaching and Learning via Symbolic Distillation of Neural A-life Agents
result.summary: Neural networks controlling behavior of A-life agents can evolve over multiple generations. While effective in making the agents survive, such networks are generally opaque to a human observer. Furthermore, the neural weights cannot be transferred between agents with different neural architectures. Distilling such neural networks into compact symbolic policies can help humans understand agent behavior in A-life. Additionally, it allows the agents to share their knowledge in a compact fashion, improving population-level learning. Distilling a neural policy into a symbolic policy is typically performed by searching the space of symbolic policies to find one that approximates the neural policy. However, even with a domain-specific language the space of policies can be large, necessitating incomplete stochastic search such as genetic algorithms. Yet the distillation remains computationally expensive. We propose to instead use a transformer pre-trained on readily available random percept-action data. Doing so speeds up distillation substantially. We derive the transformer architecture via a neural architecture search. Empirical results compare different distillation methods and the influence of the symbolic space on A-life population dynamics through self-reflection and teaching and learning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究把 A-life 智能体中不透明的神经策略蒸馏为紧凑符号策略：先用随机感知-动作数据预训练 transformer，再由神经架构搜索确定结构，以替代遗传算法式的符号空间搜索，从而加快蒸馏，并考察符号空间对种群自我反思与教-学动态的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 用预训练模型摊销符号策略搜索、把不透明神经策略压缩为可读符号策略的思路，可能为 LVR 内部 latent 状态的可解释替代物与监督信号构造提供线索，但该工作与视觉多模态推理尚无直接联系，需核查其蒸馏保真度评价方式是否可迁移。
